program_name:
Marine Biology and Aquaculture. This is the official English denomination registered in the SUA-CdS course framework (Ordinamento 2025-26, "Informazioni generali sul Corso di Studi": "Nome del corso in inglese: Marine Biology and Aquaculture"). The parallel Italian legal denomination is "Biologia Marina e Acquacoltura" ("Nome del corso in italiano" in the same SUA-CdS record); the Department of Biology, the University course record and the body of the Ordinamento more often write it with the elided article as "Biologia Marina ed Acquacoltura", and both spellings refer to the same degree. University course code: P59 (www.corsi.unina.it/P59); AlmaLaurea/MIUR codicione 0630107300700004.

STANDALONE PROGRAMME, NOT A CURRICULUM. It has its own SUA-CdS record, its own Ordinamento (new ordinamento approved for a.y. 2025-26), its own Didactic Regulations ("Regulations in force since the academic year 2025/26"), and its own Didactic Coordination Commission (CCD). Didactic Regulations, Art. 1: "This Regulation sets the organizational aspects of the Study Course in 'Marine Biology and Aquaculture' (class LM-6 - Biology). The Study Course in Marine Biology and Aquaculture belongs to the Department of Biology and is taught in English." Promoted and delivered by the Department of Biology (Dipartimento di Biologia), School of Polytechnic and Basic Sciences (Scuola Politecnica e delle Scienze di Base). Duration 2 years, 120 CFU/ECTS.

INTERNAL STRUCTURE: TWO CURRICULA, ONE DEGREE. The programme is a single LM-6 degree divided into two curricula. Didactic Regulations, Annex 1.2 (Study Plan): "The course is divided into two curricula called Marine Biology and Marine Resource Management respectively as shown in the diagram below. The First Year First Semester is common to the 2 Curricula." The study-plan headings themselves name them "Curriculum Marine Biology" and "Curriculum Aquaculture and Marine Resource Management"; the orientamento.unina.it course sheet gives them as "1) Marine Biology 2) Aquaculture and Management of marine resources". BOTH curricula are taught in English, so the choice of curriculum has no language consequence. The curriculum must be chosen at enrolment (Department page: "Students can choose the curriculum upon enrollment"; orientamento: "The choice of curriculum must be made at the time of enrollment in the Master's Degree").

RELATIONSHIP TO THE DISCONTINUED PROGRAMME (the key disambiguation requested in the research brief). This programme is the CURRENT, ACTIVE LM-6 marine degree of Federico II and must not be confused with "Biology and Ecology of the Marine Environment and Sustainable Use of Marine Resources" (Italian: "Biologia ed Ecologia dell'ambiente marino ed uso sostenibile delle sue risorse"), whose own orientamento.unina.it page is headed "Biology and Ecology of the Marine Environment and Sustainable Use of Marine (Corso attivo fino all'A.A. 2020/2021)" - i.e. active only up to a.y. 2020/2021. The two are easy to confuse because the discontinued page carries exactly the same identifying tags (Degree class LM-6, Admission Libero, Language ENG, Department Biologia) and is still online.

The official record shows CONTINUITY OF THE SAME COURSE RECORD RATHER THAN AN UNRELATED NEW COURSE: the current programme's own SUA-CdS Ordinamento, in QUADRO A1.a ("Consultazione con le organizzazioni rappresentative ... (Istituzione del corso)"), still reproduces the founding consultation carried out under the OLD name - "L'Ordine Nazionale dei Biologi e stato invitato ad esprimere un parere sull'istituzione del nuovo Corso di laurea Magistrale in 'Biologia ed Ecologia dell'ambiente marino ed uso sostenibile delle sue risorse' da attivare presso l'Universita di Napoli Federico II" - and immediately follows it with the heading "Nuove consultazioni con le parti sociali per le modifiche di ordinamento apportate per l'a.a. 2021/2022". Read together with the old page's "active until a.y. 2020/2021" tag and with the Department's earliest Marine Biology and Aquaculture regulations file ("Regolamento del CdS LM Biologia Marina ed Acquacoltura 2021-2022"), this shows the degree was restructured and renamed with effect from a.y. 2021/2022. Practical consequence for an applicant: only "Marine Biology and Aquaculture" can be applied to today; course content, study plan and curricula were reorganised at the rename, so syllabus information published under the old name is obsolete.
level:
Master (second-cycle) - Italian "Laurea Magistrale", 2-year Master's degree (laurea magistrale biennale), 120 CFU (University Educational Credits / ECTS), 4 semesters. Entry qualification required: "Laurea I Livello" (first-level/bachelor's degree, three-year), as stated in the orientamento.unina.it course sheet header ("Degree required Laurea I Livello").

Didactic Regulations, Art. 9(1): "The legal duration of the Degree Program is 2 years. The student must acquire 120 CFU, attributable to the following Types of Training Activities (TAF)" - A) basic, B) characterising, C) related or supplementary, D) at the student's choice, E) final exam, F) further training activities. Art. 9(2): "The degree is awarded after having acquired 120 CFU by passing examinations, not exceeding 12, including the final, and the performance of other training activities." The SUA-CdS Ordinamento confirms: "CFU totali per il conseguimento del titolo: 120".

CREDIT SHAPE. Each CFU = 25 hours of total student workload; in this programme lectures, seminars and laboratory/field activities are all delivered at 8 contact hours per CFU (Didactic Regulations, Art. 6). The thesis alone is worth 30 CFU (Study Plan: "Thesis Activity - 30 credits - 750 hours - In-person - Final test - Mandatory"), an unusually large final-project block that makes the second year heavily research-based. Teaching is conventional/in-presence (SUA-CdS: "Modalita di svolgimento: a. Corso di studio convenzionale"; Didactic Regulations, Art. 7: "The didactic activity is carried out in conventional modality").

Award: Dottore Magistrale in class LM-6. The degree gives access, after the State Examination, to the regulated profession of Biologist - orientamento.unina.it: "The course prepares you for the profession of biologist, as regulated by Law 24 May 1967, n. 396 and by the Presidential Decree of 5 June 2001, n. 328, after passing the State Exam." The final examination is a public defence of a thesis, marked out of 110 with the possibility of honours (Didactic Regulations, Art. 16). Attendance at lectures is "strongly recommended but not compulsory", except where a course sheet states otherwise and for credit-bearing seminars, where attendance IS compulsory (Art. 10).
teaching_language:
English - 100% English-medium, confirmed by five independent official sources with no conflicting evidence.
(a) orientamento.unina.it course sheet header: "Language ENG" (not the "ITA/ENG" tag Federico II uses for its bilingual programmes such as Ingegneria Chimica / Chemical Engineering).
(b) SUA-CdS Ordinamento 2025-26, general information block: "Lingua in cui si tiene il corso: Inglese".
(c) Didactic Regulations, Art. 1: "The Study Course in Marine Biology and Aquaculture belongs to the Department of Biology and is taught in English." Art. 4 repeats: "The course is delivered in English; therefore the student must have an adequate knowledge of the English language (level B2)."
(d) Department of Biology programme page: "The course is held in English, therefore the student must have an adequate knowledge of the English language (level B2)."
(e) international.unina.it International Courses Catalogue lists it among the 2-year Master's degrees under "Mathematics, Physics and Natural Sciences" as "Marine Biology and Aquaculture - ENG".

Every taught course in the published study plan - both curricula, both years - is delivered in English; no Italian-taught module appears anywhere in the plan. Both curricula are English-taught, so unlike Federico II's curriculum-based bilingual degrees there is no risk of choosing an Italian-language track by mistake.

ITALIAN APPEARS ONLY AS A CREDIT-BEARING SUPPORT FOR FOREIGN STUDENTS, NOT AS A TEACHING LANGUAGE. The 6-CFU "further training activities" block (TAF F, second year) is labelled in Annex 2.2 with "Activity language: English/Italian", and is defined as: "For Italian students: other knowledge useful for job placement; IT and telematics skills; training and orientation periods ... for foreign students: acquisition of Italian language knowledge." The study-plan footnote makes the split explicit: "for foreign students: 3 CFU for Italian language acquisition and 3 CFU for knowledge useful for job placement". The orientamento sheet states the same from the internship angle: "For foreign students, the credits available for the internship are a maximum of 3, while a further 3 credits are dedicated to the acquisition of the Italian language." So an international student earns 3 CFU by learning some Italian - a supported, credit-rewarded activity, not an admission barrier.

Learning outcomes are explicitly framed in English: the Ordinamento requires graduates to "utilizzare fluentemente, in forma scritta e orale, la lingua inglese con riferimento anche ai lessici disciplinari" and to write technical reports "in italiano ed in inglese"; "L'abilita di comunicazione in lingua inglese e esercitata e valutata nelle prove di" the taught courses.

CAVEAT FOR APPLICANTS: the English-medium teaching does not extend to the administrative layer. The Department of Biology's own programme page is a mixed Italian/English page; the SegrePass enrolment portal, the University enrolment guide (Guida rapida 2026/27) and the fee rules are published in Italian only.
campus:
CONFIRMED - Complesso Universitario di Monte Sant'Angelo, Edificio 7 (Department of Biology), Via Cinthia 26, 80126 Napoli, Italy. This resolves the "campus: to be verified" flag in the research brief. It is inside the city of Naples (Fuorigrotta/Soccavo area, western Naples), on the University's main science campus - NOT one of the outlying sites (Portici, San Giovanni a Teduccio, Frullone) and not the Policlinico or the historic centre.

EVIDENCE. (1) The orientamento.unina.it course sheet's "Directions" tab contains a single embedded Google map pinned to "Universita Degli Studi di Napoli Federico II Complesso Universitario di Monte Sant'Angelo" (coordinates approx. 40.8388 N, 14.1828 E); the sheet publishes no other teaching address. (2) The Department of Biology's official letterhead, as printed on its published admission documents, reads: "Sede Amministrativa: Complesso Universitario Monte Sant'Angelo - Edificio 7 - Via Cinthia, 26 - 80126 NAPOLI - ITALIA - Tel. +39 081679000 - 081679229 - 081679228 - Fax +39 081679233". (3) The Department's programme page gives the Course Coordinator's office as "Complesso Universitario di Monte S. Angelo, Universita degli Studi di Napoli Federico II, Edificio 7, via Cinthia - 80126 NAPOLI, Stanza: 0D-15a". (4) The Department's own page summarises the location as "Department of Biology, Complesso Universitario di Monte S. Angelo, Naples".

PRACTICAL NOTE ON THE ADDRESS NUMBER: unina.it pages give the street as both "via Cinthia" without a number (orientamento, coordinator's office) and "Via Cinthia, 26" (department letterhead); Monte Sant'Angelo is a single large campus addressed along Via Cinthia (commonly 21 or 26 depending on the entrance/building), so this is a signage detail rather than a discrepancy about where the programme is taught.

TEACHING IS NOT CONFINED TO THE CLASSROOM. The study plan includes a mandatory 6-CFU "Scientific Diving" course (BIO/05) taught as "Frontal lesson and practice", and the Ordinamento and orientamento both stress field and laboratory work in the marine environment. The programme's field and laboratory activity is underpinned by a partnership with the Stazione Zoologica Anton Dohrn of Naples, and orientamento.unina.it lists the network available to students: "the Stazione Zoologica of Napoli Anton Dhorn, the Istituto Superiore per la Protezione e la Ricerca Ambientale ISPRA, the Acquario of Cattolica, the Echinoidea s.r.l. Procida, Aquaculture Farm, the Arpa Puglia, the European Marine Biological Resource Centre, the Centro de Estudos do Ambiente e do Mar CESAM (Portugal), the Whitney Laboratory For Marine Bioscience, Marine Biological Laboratory (Florida, USA)" [typo "Dhorn" as published]. These are partner/field sites, not alternative campuses: no unina.it page assigns timetabled teaching to any address other than Monte Sant'Angelo.

COMPETENT STUDENT OFFICE (a different address from the teaching campus): Segreteria Studenti Area Didattica Scienze MM.FF.NN. - https://www.unina.it/-/769598-segreteria-studenti-area-didattica-scienze-mm-ff-nn- - e-mail segrmmff@unina.it. This is the office to which the English B2 certificate must be sent and, for non-EU citizens, where enrolment is done in person.
degree_class:
LM-6 - Italian degree class LM-6, "Classe delle Lauree Magistrali in Biologia" (Master's Degrees in Biology). The brief's value is CONFIRMED by four official sources: the orientamento.unina.it course sheet header ("Degree class LM-6"); the Didactic Regulations header ("MARINE BIOLOGY AND AQUACULTURE - CLASS LM-6 - School: Polytechnic of Basic Sciences - Department: Biology") and Art. 1 ("class LM-6 - Biology"); the SUA-CdS Ordinamento ("Classe: LM-6 Classe delle Lauree Magistrali in Biologia"); and the AlmaLaurea transparency record ("marine biology and aquaculture - biologia marina ed acquacoltura (LM-6)").

No "R" suffix or other ministerial variant is used for this course (unlike, for example, Federico II's LM-86 R Precision Livestock Farming). Note that LM-6 is the general Biology master's class, not a marine-specific class: Federico II runs more than one LM-6 degree in the Department of Biology, so degree class alone does not identify this programme - and, critically, the DISCONTINUED "Biology and Ecology of the Marine Environment and Sustainable Use of Marine Resources" was ALSO LM-6. Applicants and data pipelines must therefore match on the course NAME (or on the course code P59), never on "LM-6 + English + Biology" alone.

Because the class is LM-6 Biologia, the degree confers eligibility for the State Examination for the profession of Biologist (Section A of the Albo dei Biologi), per Law 396/1967 and D.P.R. 328/2001. The Ordinamento records that the National Order of Biologists was formally consulted and gave a favourable opinion on the course's institution ("L'Ordine dei Biologi esprime parere favorevole all'attivazione di detto Corso").
admission_type:
OPEN ACCESS ("Admission Libero") - there is NO numerus clausus, NO competitive ranking and NO admission bando for this programme. This is the single most important structural difference between this degree and Federico II's restricted English-taught Master's degrees (e.g. Precision Livestock Farming), and it means a qualified applicant cannot be refused for lack of places.

The orientamento.unina.it course sheet header states "Admission Libero", and the body confirms: "Access to the Degree Course is free, subject to verification of possession of the curricular and personal culture requirements as well as possession of the curricular requirements of three-year degrees in biology." The SUA-CdS Ordinamento contains no "numero programmato" or "utenza sostenibile" cap section, and the Didactic Regulations, Art. 5, leave scheduling to the CCD: "The CCD of the Master's Degree Program normally regulates the admission criteria and any scheduling of enrolments, except in the case subject to different provisions of law. Verification of personal preparation is always mandatory, and only students who meet the curricular requirements can access it."

"Open access" is NOT "automatic access". Two gates must be cleared before enrolment can proceed: (i) the CURRICULAR REQUIREMENTS (a fixed CFU profile in BIO/CHIM/FIS/MAT sectors - see academic_requirements), and (ii) the VERIFICATION OF PERSONAL PREPARATION, which is mandatory for everyone but automatically waived for applicants whose bachelor's degree mark is at least 90/110. English at B2 is a third, separate condition.

THE PROCEDURE HAS TWO DISTINCT STAGES, AND THE FIRST IS THE SAME FOR EVERY NATIONALITY. Department of Biology programme page: "To become a student of the master program there are two steps: Admission [and] Enrollment. The ADMISSION procedure is common to all the students of any nationality, and it is mandatory in order to verify the requirements and to confirm your knowledge of English. The ENROLLMENT procedure is different depending on if you are an Italian, EU or Extra-EU prospective student."

(1) ADMISSION (all nationalities). Handled directly by the Programme Coordinator, not by a portal. "Foreign students to enroll to the MD in Marine Biology and Aquaculture have to contact the Coordinator, Prof. Francesca Carella, sending a mail to: mba@unina.it". A document set (diploma, transcript, passport, CV, English certificate) is assessed, and the stage ends with a decision document: "At the end of this procedure you will obtain a Pre-Acceptance Letter from the program coordinator to be used for the Enrollment procedure and to request the VISA (when necessary)."

(2) ENROLLMENT (nationality-dependent). "Italian and EU Students will need to enroll using SegrePass while Extra-EU Students will need to enroll through https://www.universitaly.it/." The Department adds: "The enrollment procedure must first be carried out on SEGREPASS and then the model R must be sent." Note that under the University's general rules ALL students of foreign citizenship - EU included - must complete enrolment at the Student Office counter rather than online: Guida rapida 2026/27, "Iscrizione per gli studenti con cittadinanza straniera": "Coloro che presentano una cittadinanza straniera dovranno effettuare l'iscrizione presso gli sportelli delle Segreterie Studenti, non potranno usare la procedura on-line."

NO TOLC, NO SAT, NO WRITTEN ENTRANCE EXAMINATION, no portfolio and no merit ranking of any kind. There is also no application fee, because there is no competition to apply to.
academic_requirements:
ENTRY QUALIFICATION. A three-year bachelor's degree (laurea triennale), a three-year university diploma, or an equivalent foreign qualification recognised as suitable. Didactic Regulations, Art. 4: "Students wishing to enrol in the master's degree Course in Marine Biology and Aquaculture must be in possession of a bachelor's degree or a three-year university diploma or another qualification obtained abroad, recognised as suitable according to current regulations. Students must also be in possession of the minimum curricular requirements and adequate personal preparation."

A) CURRICULAR REQUIREMENTS - AUTOMATIC ROUTE. Satisfied by demonstrating the knowledge of the Italian three-year degree class L-13 (Scienze Biologiche), or class 12 under the older D.M. 509/1999. Didactic Regulations, Art. 4: "The student must demonstrate that he/she has acquired the knowledge of the three-year degree in class L-13 (i.e. class 12 ex D.M. 509)."

B) CURRICULAR REQUIREMENTS - CREDIT ROUTE (all other degree classes, and in practice every foreign bachelor's degree). Applicants from other classes must hold knowledge in the BIO/, CHIM/, FIS/ and MAT/ scientific-disciplinary sectors, evidenced by a FIXED and CUMULATIVE credit profile. Didactic Regulations, Art. 4 (identical in the 2024-25 and the current 2025/26 versions, and identical in the SUA-CdS Ordinamento and on the orientamento and Department pages): "Students from other degree classes must have knowledge in the SSDs BIO/, CHIM/, FIS/, MAT/. Curricular requirements are determined by having acquired: 1) At least 18 CFU in the fields BIO/01-3, BIO/05, BIO/06, BIO/07. 2) At least 6 CFU in the sectors BIO/04, BIO/09, BIO/10, BIO/11, BIO/18, BIO/19. 3) At least 6 CFU in the sectors CHIM/01-06; at least 12 CFU in the sectors MAT/01-09, FIS/01-08."

That is 42 CFU minimum in total, in four separate buckets - all four must be satisfied independently; a surplus in one does not offset a shortfall in another. The Department publishes the same thresholds translated out of SSD codes into plain subject names, which is the more usable form for a foreign applicant mapping a non-Italian transcript:
  - "At least 18 ECTS in the sectors Botany, Zoology, Comparative Anatomy and Cytology, Ecology" (BIO/01-03 Botany and Plant Physiology / BIO/05 Zoology / BIO/06 Comparative Anatomy and Cytology / BIO/07 Ecology);
  - "At least 6 ECTS in the sectors Vegetal physiology, Physiology, Biochemistry, Molecular Biology, Genetic, Microbiology" (BIO/04, BIO/09, BIO/10, BIO/11, BIO/18, BIO/19);
  - "At least 6 credits in the Chemistry sectors" (CHIM/01-06);
  - "At least 12 ECTS in the sectors Mathematic, Physic" (MAT/01-09, FIS/01-08).

The 12-CFU Mathematics/Physics bucket is the one that most often disqualifies otherwise strong marine-biology and environmental-science applicants, since many foreign biology bachelor's degrees carry less than 12 ECTS of combined maths and physics. There is no published mechanism for making up a shortfall before enrolment (no OFA route is defined for this Master's), so the profile should be checked against the transcript before applying.

C) VERIFICATION OF ADEQUATE PERSONAL PREPARATION - MANDATORY FOR EVERYONE, BUT WAIVED ON A GRADE THRESHOLD. Didactic Regulations, Art. 5: "Verification of personal preparation is always mandatory, and only students who meet the curricular requirements can access it. The verification methods will be redefined annually by the CCD and published on the web site of the Department of Biology." The operative threshold is published by the Department: "Graduates who have obtained the degree with a grade of not less than 90/110 are exempted from the test to verify the adequacy of personal preparation."

HOW THE VERIFICATION IS ACTUALLY RUN (orientamento.unina.it, current sheet): "All enrolled students, including those coming from Federico II, in possession of the curricular requirements and a three-year degree qualification with a score lower than 90/110, will be subjected to verification of the adequacy of their personal preparation. ... The verification is based in the first instance on an analysis, by the Master's Degree Study Plans and Admissions Commission appointed by the CCD, of the student's previous curriculum and the scores achieved in the BIO sector exams and does not involve direct involvement of the students. If the Commission deems it appropriate, it will carry out an oral interview for evaluation purposes. The Commission reserves the right to exempt from the evaluation interview candidates in possession of particularly important qualifications or a certificate of passing of further supplementary exams taken." So the default is a DESK REVIEW of the transcript, with an interview only if the Commission wants one - and it is a pass/fail eligibility check, never a competitive score.

PROCEDURAL TRAP (EU/Italian route): the orientamento sheet states that the secretariat forwards the verification request to the Coordinator only after the student has already registered and paid: "The secretariat will be responsible for sending the application via email to the Coordinator and via CC to the student ... for the secretariat to proceed with forwarding the application the student must have registered and paid university fees." Payment therefore precedes the personal-preparation check on that route. Foreign applicants avoid this by going through the Coordinator-led Admission stage first (mba@unina.it), which produces a Pre-Acceptance Letter before any enrolment or payment.

D) ENGLISH B2 - a separate hard requirement for all applicants; see language_requirements.

E) NOTE ON GRADE CONVERSION. The 90/110 waiver is expressed on the Italian scale and no unina.it page publishes a conversion table for foreign marks, so applicants with a non-Italian degree should expect the Admissions Commission to assess the transcript directly rather than apply an arithmetic conversion.
entry_exam_or_test:
NO entrance examination, NO TOLC, NO SAT, NO written admission test, NO portfolio, NO competitive interview and NO merit ranking. Access is open ("Admission Libero"), so nothing a candidate does is scored against other candidates. Three assessments nevertheless exist, and ALL of them are pass/fail eligibility checks:

1) CURRICULAR-REQUIREMENTS CHECK (documentary). A desk verification that the transcript carries the required 18 + 6 + 6 + 12 CFU in the prescribed BIO/CHIM/MAT/FIS sectors. Performed on the submitted transcript; no test is sat.

2) VERIFICATION OF PERSONAL PREPARATION (desk review, with a possible oral interview). MANDATORY IN PRINCIPLE FOR ALL - Didactic Regulations, Art. 5: "Verification of personal preparation is always mandatory, and only students who meet the curricular requirements can access it" - but AUTOMATICALLY WAIVED for anyone whose bachelor's degree mark is 90/110 or above (Department of Biology: "Graduates who have obtained the degree with a grade of not less than 90/110 are exempted from the test to verify the adequacy of personal preparation"). For those below 90/110, orientamento.unina.it describes a document-based first instance: the Master's Degree Study Plans and Admissions Commission analyses "the student's previous curriculum and the scores achieved in the BIO sector exams and does not involve direct involvement of the students. If the Commission deems it appropriate, it will carry out an oral interview for evaluation purposes." The Commission may also waive the interview for candidates with "particularly important qualifications or a certificate of passing of further supplementary exams taken". The methods are re-set annually by the CCD and published on the Department of Biology website, so the current year's notice should always be checked.

3) ENGLISH PLACEMENT TEST (only if no B2 certificate is held). Department of Biology: "Students who are NOT in possession of a B2 Level English Language Certification will be subjected to verification, by means of an interview or test, the methods of which will be indicated from time to time by the CCD." The University-level implementation is the CLA placement test: the Department's English-certification notice states that "Students regularly enrolled in the first year who do not have a B2 level English language certification must take the Placement test", accessed through the ESOL.UNINA platform with university e-mail credentials and password, and administered by the Centro Linguistico di Ateneo (CLA, https://www.cla.unina.it/home). See language_requirements for the timing caveat.

WHAT REPLACES AN ENTRANCE EXAM FOR FOREIGN APPLICANTS: the Coordinator-led ADMISSION procedure. It is documentary, not an examination - the Department lists the file to be submitted (bachelor diploma, transcript of records, passport copy, updated CV, English certificate where available, other relevant documents) and states its output: "At the end of this procedure you will obtain a Pre-Acceptance Letter from the program coordinator to be used for the Enrollment procedure and to request the VISA (when necessary)." No interview is mentioned as a standard step, no scoring grid is published, and no deadline for this stage is published - contact mba@unina.it early.

CONTRAST WORTH KNOWING: within the very same Department of Biology, the BACHELOR programme "Biology for One-Health" DOES run a formal non-EU selection - a published Call for Applications (23 June 2026), an "Interview schedule A.Y. 2026/2027 (non-EU candidates)" and a published "List of the admitted candidates for the academic year 2026-2027 ... after the interviews" (Public Notice dated 6 July 2026). NOTHING equivalent is published for Marine Biology and Aquaculture. Do not assume the Biology for One-Health call, its interview dates or its admitted list apply to this Master's - they do not.
seats_total:
NO SEAT LIMIT - the programme is open access and no maximum number of places is published anywhere on unina.it. This is a positive finding rather than a missing one: orientamento.unina.it states "Admission Libero" in the course-sheet header and "Access to the Degree Course is free, subject to verification of possession of the curricular and personal culture requirements"; the SUA-CdS Ordinamento contains no numero programmato / utenza sostenibile cap; and the Didactic Regulations contain no cap, no ranking provision and no reference to a competition. There is consequently no admission bando, no graduatoria (merit ranking) and no scorrimenti (ranking slides) for this course.

Practical meaning for an applicant: meeting the curricular requirements, clearing the personal-preparation check and holding English B2 is sufficient - a qualified candidate is not competing for a finite number of places. The only real capacity constraint visible in the documentation is pedagogical rather than administrative: the mandatory 6-CFU "Scientific Diving" course involves practical in-water work, and laboratory/field activities are credited at 8 contact hours per CFU, which implies small-group organisation, but no published rule converts this into an admission cap.

The absence of a number should not be read as an absence of process: enrolment still has to be completed within the University's calendar (see application_deadline_eu) and, for non-EU applicants residing abroad, within the Universitaly/visa timetable, which is the genuine practical bottleneck for this programme.
non_eu_reserved_seats:
[uncertain] NO reserved non-EU quota is published for this programme on any unina.it source, and because the programme is open access there is no admission decree in which such a quota would normally be stated. For Federico II's restricted-access courses the reserved non-EU figure is set in the annual Rectoral admission decree (e.g. "numero 15 posti riservati a cittadini non comunitari residenti all'estero" for Precision Livestock Farming); Marine Biology and Aquaculture has no such decree at all, so there is no document in which a reserved figure could appear.

What IS documented is a separate PROCEDURE for non-EU citizens residing abroad, not a separate quota: Department of Biology - "Italian and EU Students will need to enroll using SegrePass while Extra-EU Students will need to enroll through https://www.universitaly.it/", with "The Universitaly deadline for Extra-European Students application is June 15th, 2026." The preceding Admission stage (documents assessed by the Coordinator, ending in a Pre-Acceptance Letter) is expressly "common to all the students of any nationality".

Marked uncertain because: (a) as with every Italian degree, a per-course contingent for non-EU candidates residing abroad is declared each year on universitaly.it, and that figure is the one that actually governs how many visa-track students can pre-enrol - but universitaly.it lies outside the unina.it-only source restriction set for this research and was deliberately not consulted; (b) the University's own summary sheet for that contingent, "UniversItaly 2026/2027 - Information for NON EU Students with residency abroad" (https://www.unina.it/documents/20117/4260320/UniversItaly_2026_27.pdf), is published as a PDF whose embedded fonts carry no Unicode mapping, so its text could not be extracted for verification; (c) no Department of Biology or international.unina.it page states a number for this course. A prospective non-EU applicant should therefore treat the Universitaly course sheet as the authoritative source for the contingent and, in parallel, contact the Coordinator at mba@unina.it early.
language_requirements:
ENGLISH - B2 (CEFR). Compulsory for ALL applicants of every nationality; it is an eligibility condition, not a scored criterion. The requirement is stated identically in every official source:
  - Didactic Regulations, Art. 4: "The course is delivered in English; therefore the student must have an adequate knowledge of the English language (level B2)."
  - SUA-CdS Ordinamento, QUADRO A3.a: "Il corso e erogato in lingua inglese, per cui lo studente deve possedere una adeguata conoscenza della lingua inglese (livello B2). Le modalita di verifica della personale preparazione e del livello B2 di Inglese per l'accesso al Corso di Laurea Magistrale sono riportate nel regolamento didattico del corso di studio e rese note sul sito WEB del Dipartimento di Biologia."
  - orientamento.unina.it: "The course is taught in English, so the student must have adequate knowledge of the English language (level B2)."
  - Department of Biology: "The course is held in English, therefore the student must have an adequate knowledge of the English language (level B2)."

TWO ROUTES TO SATISFY IT, AND THE FILING INSTRUCTION IS EXPLICIT.
(1) HOLD A B2 CERTIFICATE. Department of Biology: "NOTICE!!! Students in possession of the ENGLISH LANGUAGE CERTIFICATION LEVEL B2 must deliver it or send it by email, in pdf, format to the administrative contact of the Student Secretariat of Sciences MFN, sent a mail to segrmmff@unina.it" [wording as published]. The certificate is ALSO one of the documents named for the Coordinator-led Admission stage ("the certificate of English language (when available/necessary)", to mba@unina.it) - so international applicants send it twice, to two different addresses, for two different purposes.
(2) SIT THE UNIVERSITY PLACEMENT TEST. Department of Biology: "Students who are NOT in possession of a B2 Level English Language Certification will be subjected to verification, by means of an interview or test, the methods of which will be indicated from time to time by the CCD." The University implementation is the CLA placement test: "Students regularly enrolled in the first year who do not have a B2 level English language certification must take the Placement test", taken through the ESOL.UNINA platform using university e-mail credentials and password, run by the Centro Linguistico di Ateneo (https://www.cla.unina.it/home).

IMPORTANT TIMING CAVEAT: the placement-test notice is addressed to students "regularly enrolled in the first year" - i.e. the test is sat AFTER enrolment, not before it. It is therefore not a realistic substitute for a certificate for a non-EU applicant, who needs evidence of English before the Pre-Acceptance Letter and before the visa interview. In practice a non-EU applicant should treat a paper B2 certificate as necessary, even though the University formally allows the test alternative.

NO ACCEPTED-CERTIFICATE LIST AND NO SCORE TABLE IS PUBLISHED. No unina.it or Department page names which certificates are accepted (IELTS / TOEFL / Cambridge / Trinity ...) or maps their scores onto B2; the requirement is expressed purely in CEFR terms and the judgement is left to the Secretariat and the CCD. international.unina.it adds the visa-side reason to hold one anyway: an international certificate of English "is useful for the issue of the visa by the diplomatic/consular Representation."

ITALIAN - NOT REQUIRED FOR ADMISSION. Because the programme is registered as English-taught, the University's central rule applies (international.unina.it): for a degree course taught in ENGLISH, "level B2 Italian language proficiency is not required." The CLIQ-system Italian B2 certificate and the Italian proficiency test apply only to Italian-taught programmes.

ITALIAN IS, HOWEVER, BUILT INTO THE CURRICULUM AS A CREDIT-BEARING ACTIVITY FOR FOREIGN STUDENTS. The second-year 6-CFU "further training activities" block is defined so that "for foreign students: acquisition of Italian language knowledge", split by the study-plan footnote as "3 CFU for Italian language acquisition and 3 CFU for knowledge useful for job placement" (orientamento states the same: "For foreign students, the credits available for the internship are a maximum of 3, while a further 3 credits are dedicated to the acquisition of the Italian language"). Italian will also matter in daily practice: the SegrePass portal, the enrolment guide, the fee rules and much of the Department's own site are Italian-only.

A) ADMISSION STAGE - the only list published specifically for this programme, and it applies to ALL nationalities (submitted to the Coordinator at mba@unina.it). THE HEADLINE FOR AN INTERNATIONAL APPLICANT: TUITION IS EFFECTIVELY FREE, AND THE TWO PUBLISHED SCHEMES DO RECONCILE. The Guida rapida 2026/27 grants blanket exemptions by citizenship: (e) "stranieri (cittadinanza in Paesi extra UE): sono esonerati totalmente dal pagamento del contributo di iscrizione; devono versare solo la tassa regionale per il diritto allo studio ... e l'imposta di bollo, entro il termine ordinario di scadenza per il versamento della I rata"; (f) "europei (cittadinanza in altri Paesi UE): sono tenuti solo al versamento di un contributo fisso pari a 200 EUR per l'iscrizione, se l'importo del contributo dovuto sia pari o superiore a 200 EUR. Se inferiore, possono effettuare l'iscrizione nella modalita ordinaria." This is exactly the flat scheme advertised on international.unina.it ("European students EUR 200/year (tuition fees) + regional tax + EUR 16.00 legal stamp; Non-european students regional fee + EUR 16.00 legal stamp"), so the two documents agree in substance. Net cost for a non-EU student: the regional tax plus a EUR 16 stamp - on the order of EUR 150-190 per year.

REGIONAL TAX FOR THE RIGHT TO STUDY (compulsory, three bands for 2026/27): EUR 130.00 for ISEEU up to EUR 25,500 "e per gli studenti appartenenti ai Paesi particolarmente poveri, ex art. 13 comma 5 DPCM 9 aprile 2001 (D.M. n. 176 del 24 febbraio 2026)"; EUR 151.00 for ISEEU between EUR 25,500.01 and EUR 51,000 "e per gli studenti con nucleo familiare residente all'estero"; EUR 173.00 for ISEEU above EUR 51,000 or where no ISEEU is filed. A typical international student whose family resides abroad therefore falls in the EUR 151.00 band, unless their country is on the D.M. 176/2026 list of particularly poor countries, in which case EUR 130.00 applies. Plus EUR 16.00 stamp duty.

STANDARD ISEEU SCHEME (for students assessed on Italian income). First-year students pay a "contributo agevolato": fully exempt up to ISEEU EUR 30,000 (no-tax area); above that, a fixed component of EUR 1,011.50 plus a variable component, to a maximum of EUR 2,384.00 for those filing no ISEEU declaration. Payment in three instalments: 60% + regional tax + stamp duty from 16 July (or 1 September) and by 2 November 2026; 20% by 1 March 2027; 20% by 30 April 2027. A 50% reduction applies to a first-year Master's student who obtained the bachelor's degree by October of the third in-course year with 110 e lode.

OTHER COSTS THAT CAN ARISE ON THIS PROGRAMME. Single course (corso singolo): EUR 180 each - relevant because enrolling in the Master's after 31 December 2026 may require first earning 6-12 CFU this way (refundable if taken at Federico II and the Master's enrolment is completed by 31 March 2027). Incoming/outgoing transfer or career transcription: EUR 96. Late enrolment surcharge: EUR 50 to 15 January 2027, EUR 110 from 16 January 2027; EUR 100 more from 16 July 2027 for unpaid second/third instalments. Duplicate parchment: EUR 52. Career suspension: EUR 202. There is NO application fee, because there is no admission competition. Scholarship route worth checking: the University's "Study in Naples" call for international students, publicised on the Department of Biology's own noticeboard (https://www.international.unina.it/).

uncertainty_notes:
1) IDENTITY IS CONFIRMED AND THE DISAMBIGUATION IN THE BRIEF IS CORRECT. "Marine Biology and Aquaculture" (LM-6, course code P59, Department of Biology) is the current, active programme, with 2025/26 Didactic Regulations and a 2025-26 Ordinamento. The discontinued "Biology and Ecology of the Marine Environment and Sustainable Use of Marine Resources" carries the explicit tag "Corso attivo fino all'A.A. 2020/2021" on its own orientamento page. The confusion risk is real and high: BOTH pages are still live, and both display Degree class LM-6, Admission Libero, Language ENG, Department Biologia. Match on programme name or on code P59 - never on class + language + department.

2) THE TWO ARE THE SAME COURSE RECORD, RENAMED - not two unrelated degrees. The current programme's SUA-CdS Ordinamento still carries the founding consultation conducted under the old name and then flags "Nuove consultazioni con le parti sociali per le modifiche di ordinamento apportate per l'a.a. 2021/2022"; the Department's earliest Marine Biology and Aquaculture regulations file is dated 2021-2022, immediately after the old course's last year (2020/2021). Consequence: syllabus, study plan and curricula published under the old name are obsolete and must not be reused, even though the institutional lineage is continuous.

3) CAMPUS FLAG RESOLVED. The brief listed campus as "to be verified"; it is Complesso Universitario di Monte Sant'Angelo, Edificio 7, Via Cinthia 26, 80126 Napoli. The only residual imprecision is the street number (unina.it pages give "via Cinthia" with no number and "Via Cinthia, 26"; the campus is also commonly addressed at Via Cinthia 21), which is a signage detail, not a disagreement about location. Partner institutions (Stazione Zoologica Anton Dohrn and others) host field and laboratory work but are not alternative campuses; no unina.it page assigns timetabled teaching to any other address.

4) ENROLMENT-WINDOW CONFLICT (resolved in favour of the University guide). The orientamento course sheet says enrolment "usually take[s] place from 1 September to 31 October of each year"; the Guida rapida all'iscrizione 2026/27 sets 16 July / 1 September to 2 November 2026, an extraordinary period from 3 November with surcharges, and an outer limit of 31 March 2027 for first-year Master's enrolment. The guide is the operative document for a.y. 2026/27 and the sheet defers to it; the sheet's sentence appears to be generic boilerplate. The guide itself adds "Nota: le date di scadenza possono essere soggette a variazioni."

5) NON-EU APPLICATION TIMETABLE IS THE WEAKEST POINT IN THE PUBLISHED RECORD. The 15 June 2026 Universitaly deadline is stated clearly on the Department page, but the stage that must PRECEDE it - the Coordinator-led Admission procedure ending in a Pre-Acceptance Letter - has no published opening date, closing date or turnaround time. Note also that the international.unina.it post-15-June extension applies only to RESTRICTED-ACCESS programmes, so it does NOT rescue a late applicant to this open-access course. Write to mba@unina.it months in advance.

6) CONTRADICTION ON THE VISA LETTER. The Department promises a "Pre-Acceptance Letter from the program coordinator ... to request the VISA", while international.unina.it states "The University of Naples Federico II does not issue admission letters for obtaining a visa." A departmental pre-acceptance letter is formally not a central admission letter, but consulates may not accept the distinction. Obtain the Coordinator's letter; do not expect anything from the central administration.

7) ENGLISH PLACEMENT TEST IS POST-ENROLMENT. The Department's placement-test notice addresses "Students regularly enrolled in the first year", i.e. the test is sat after enrolment. For a non-EU applicant who needs evidence of English at the Pre-Acceptance and visa stages, the certificate route is in practice the only workable one, even though the University formally offers the alternative. No accepted-certificate list and no IELTS/TOEFL/Cambridge score mapping is published anywhere on unina.it.

8) NO NON-EU QUOTA IS PUBLISHED ON UNINA.IT, and none could exist in a bando because there is no bando. The per-course non-EU contingent declared annually on universitaly.it was deliberately not consulted under the unina.it-only source restriction. The University's own summary, UniversItaly_2026_27.pdf, could not be read (see point 11).

9) FEE FIGURE MISMATCH (minor, and partly resolved). international.unina.it gives a flat regional tax of "EUR 140/year", which matches none of the three 2026/27 bands (EUR 130 / 151 / 173) in the Guida rapida - the international page appears not to have been updated for a.y. 2026/27. The more important point is that the two schemes DO reconcile in substance: the Guida's citizenship-based exemptions (non-EU citizens fully exempt from the contribution; other-EU citizens a flat EUR 200) are precisely what international.unina.it advertises. Expect roughly EUR 150-190/year total for a non-EU student. Use calcolatrice.unina.it for a binding figure.

10) CURRICULUM NAMING IS INCONSISTENT ACROSS OFFICIAL SOURCES (cosmetic). The second curriculum appears as "Marine Resource Management" (Regulations, introductory sentence), "Aquaculture and Marine Resource Management" (Regulations, study-plan headings) and "Aquaculture and Management of marine resources" (orientamento sheet). All three denote the same track. Similarly, the Italian course name appears as both "Biologia Marina e Acquacoltura" (SUA-CdS field) and "Biologia Marina ed Acquacoltura" (Department pages, Ordinamento body).

11) TECHNICAL RETRIEVAL PROBLEMS ENCOUNTERED. www.orientamento.unina.it presents an invalid TLS certificate chain to some clients and was retrievable only with certificate verification relaxed. www.corsi.unina.it/P59 renders its content via JavaScript and returns an essentially empty document to plain HTTP clients. The old University course record https://www.unina.it/-/26288210-biologia-marina-ed-acquacoltura now returns "Pagina non trovata sul vecchio portale". UniversItaly_2026_27.pdf uses subset-embedded fonts with no Unicode mapping, so its text is not machine-extractable - the non-EU dates here were therefore taken from the HTML pages on international.unina.it and from the Department page instead.

12) THE DEPARTMENT PAGE IS PARTLY STALE AND PARTLY COMPROMISED. It carries a live 2026/27 date (last modified 25/08/2026, Universitaly deadline 15 June 2026) but links a non-EU notice dated 14 March 2024, and the site footer contains injected spam text (unrelated keyword links), a sign the WordPress install has been tampered with at some point. Content was cross-checked against the Regulations, the Ordinamento and orientamento.unina.it wherever possible; no factual contradiction was found, but the page should not be treated as freshly maintained in every part. Its phone number field also displays an obvious placeholder ("+1-888-123-1234") - the real Department numbers are +39 081679000 / 081679229 / 081679228.

13) SOURCE-DOMAIN COMPLIANCE. All sources used are on unina.it hosts (unina.it, old.unina.it, orientamento.unina.it, international.unina.it, corsi.unina.it, dipartimentodibiologia.unina.it, docenti.unina.it), as required by the brief. Third-party aggregators that surfaced in search (AlmaLaurea statistiche, Mastersportal, univpm/unibo/unimi marine-biology pages) were NOT used as evidence; the single AlmaLaurea reference in degree_class is cited only as a corroborating index of the official denomination, and every substantive claim in this record rests on a unina.it source.

14) NOT VERIFIED / OUT OF SCOPE. Current-year CCD notices redefining the personal-preparation methods for a.y. 2026/27 (the Regulations say these are "redefined annually" and published on the Department site) were not located; the a.y. 2026/27 teaching calendar PDF (Calendario_didattico_AA_26_27_Scienze.pdf) was identified but its per-course dates were not extracted; and no published data on cohort size, applicant numbers or actual enrolment for this programme was found on unina.it.
